title: Balanced and unbalanced forces

draft.title: Balanced and unbalanced forces
card: Several forces can act on an object at once. What matters is the total effect of all of them together.
forces that are equal in size and opposite in direction, so they cancel out. An object at rest stays still, and a moving object keeps moving at the same speed in the same direction.
forces that do not cancel out. The object starts moving, stops, speeds up, slows down or changes direction.
A book resting on a table stays still because the push of the table up on the book balances the pull of gravity down. A bigger force one way than the other makes the forces unbalanced.
draft.remember: Balanced forces cancel and the motion stays the same. Unbalanced forces change the motion.

a.q: A cyclist rides along a flat path at a steady speed in a straight line. What can be said about the forces on the bike?
opts: They are balanced, so the motion does not change
They are unbalanced, so the bike keeps moving
They are balanced, so the bike must slow to a stop
They are unbalanced, so the bike is speeding up
a.why: A steady speed in a straight line means the motion is not changing, so the forces cancel out. Many students think a moving object needs unbalanced forces to keep going, but unbalanced forces would change the speed or direction.
a.clue: Is the speed or direction of the bike changing?

b.q: Two teams pull on opposite ends of a rope with equal force, and the rope does not move. Team A then pulls with a bigger force while Team B stays the same. What happens to the rope?
opts: It moves towards Team A because the forces are unbalanced
It stays still because the forces are still balanced
It moves towards Team B because the forces are unbalanced
It stays still because the forces are unbalanced
b.why: At first the equal, opposite pulls cancel, so the rope stays still. When Team A pulls harder the forces no longer cancel, so the rope starts to move in the direction of the bigger force, towards Team A. Team B's pull is smaller, so the rope does not go that way.
b.clue: Which team now has the bigger pull?

a.best: They are balanced, so the motion does not change

b.best: It moves towards Team A because the forces are unbalanced
